skills.name: Writing a brief account: the role of women in my culture

note.text:
An account tells about a topic clearly, with facts and examples, in a few paragraphs.
Plan: a title; an introduction (what you will write about); two or three body paragraphs, each about one role (in the family, in farming and trade, in culture and leadership), with examples; a conclusion (your opinion).
Use the simple present for things that are generally true (“Women grow most of the food crops”).
Linking words: firstly, also, in addition, moreover, finally, in conclusion.

worked_example.problem: Plan a brief account of the role of women in your culture.
steps: Title: The role of women in Bafut culture.
Introduction: women play many important roles.
Body: in the family (they care for children and the home); in the economy (they farm and trade in the market); in culture (they lead dances and women's associations).
Conclusion: women are the backbone of our society and deserve respect and education.
worked_example.answer: Title → introduction → family → economy → culture → conclusion

cards.idea: An account has an introduction, body paragraphs and a conclusion.

example: They sell their crops at the market.

cards.idea: Use linking words: firstly, also, in addition, finally.
example: In addition, women lead the njangi groups.

questions.prompt: Put the parts of the account in order.

items.text: The role of women in our culture
In our culture, women play many important roles.
Firstly, they care for the children and the home.
In addition, they grow food and trade in the market.
Finally, they lead dances and women's associations.
In conclusion, women are the backbone of our society.

paper_task.prompt: Write a brief account (about 150 words) in your exercise book about the role of women in your culture. Use paragraphs, examples and linking words.
model:
The role of women in our culture

In my village in the North West, women play many important roles.

Firstly, women care for the family. They cook, keep the home clean and look after the children and the old.

In addition, women are the main farmers. They grow maize, beans and cocoyams, and on market days they sell their crops. Many of them save money in njangi groups and pay their children's school fees.

Finally, women keep our culture alive. They lead dances at festivals, teach songs to the young and, in some places, the queen mother advises the Fon.

In conclusion, women are the backbone of our society. They deserve respect and the same chance to go to school as men.
checklist: My introduction says what I will write about.
Each body paragraph is about one role, with examples.
I used the simple present for general facts.
My sentences start with capitals and end with full stops.
